# Draft releases from tags

Pushing any tag runs workflows/tag-release.yml. The workflow checks out the tagged source and native libraries, configures signing, installs the pinned Android SDK/NDK tools, runs the script/core tests and builds every application module under versions/. It verifies the signatures and native alignment of all generated APKs before creating a GitHub release with draft=true and attaching every APK.

The workflow never publishes a release. Re-running a tag replaces APK assets only while its release is still a draft. It refuses to modify an already published release. APK files are attached directly as release assets.

## One-time signing setup

In GitHub repository Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions, add:

| Secret | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 | Base64 encoding of the complete signing keystore file |
| ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD | The keystore password |
| ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS | The signing key alias |
| ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD | The signing key password |

Use the same keystore as the APKs already distributed to users. Stable signing is necessary for Android to accept subsequent APK updates. A new random key is never generated by the workflow. Missing secrets stop the job in Configure release signing, before Java, Gradle and Android SDK setup, with a list of the missing names. No secret values are printed.

For the local development key only, this PowerShell command writes its base64 encoding to an ignored local file:

    [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path 'signing/development.jks').Path)) | Set-Content -LiteralPath 'signing/keystore-base64.txt' -Encoding ascii

Copy that file's contents into ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 through GitHub's secret editor. For production, encode the production keystore instead and use its matching credentials. Never commit keystores, signing.properties or base64 key files. The signing/ directory is already excluded from Git.

## Repository contents

Commit this project, including the imported native binaries under every version's src/main/jniLibs and the corresponding version.json and engine-provenance.json. Native libraries can be tracked with Git LFS; checkout enables LFS downloads. Do not commit the reference upstream/ checkouts, local build outputs, private signing files or device diagnostics.

The build uses Gradle Wrapper 8.13, Java 17, Android platform 36, build tools 36.0.0, NDK 29.0.14033849 and CMake 3.22.1. New versions generated from the template are discovered automatically; the workflow does not hardcode Fotg or fs2demo.

On the GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner, the workflow calls cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager inside the SDK directory, without depending on PATH. It uses ANDROID_HOME, then ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, then the runner's standard /usr/local/lib/android/sdk path. If the executable is missing, the job reports the exact path it checked.

## Create a release

1. Update the shared launcher version and each affected application's versionCode before distributing an APK update. Per-TC versionName values remain under developer control.
2. Commit and push the project changes.
3. Create and push a tag, for example:

       git tag v0.2.1
       git push origin v0.2.1

4. Open Actions to follow the build. After success, open Releases and review the new draft and its APK attachments. Publish it manually when ready.

The tag must include the workflow and all required sources/native files. The repository must permit GitHub Actions to write release contents; the release job requests contents: write.

After changing the workflow, commit and push the fix and create a new tag at that commit. Re-running a failed run uses the original tagged commit, so it will not pick up a workflow fix pushed afterward.

Local validation:

    python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
    actionlint .github/workflows/tag-release.yml

Release-helper tests replace GitHub CLI calls with mocks. They do not create a remote release or upload anything. The actual hosted workflow runs when a tag is pushed to GitHub.
